ILOSTAT compares the labour-market situation of persons with and without disabilities in 61 countries. The average is unweighted: each country contributes to the average without adjustment for population size.
The ILO specifies that these figures are based on the unweighted average of 61 countries. They are not a world rate weighted by population.
The figure comes from the unweighted average of 61 countries. This must be stated explicitly: it is not a population-weighted world rate.
The figure must remain linked to its population, territory, year and method. Separating it from that context can change its meaning.

Pay gap and disability

The pay gap associated with disability is not limited to access to employment. An international ILO study found an average difference in hourly pay even after taking variables such as age, education and occupation into account.
international subsample of 30 countries · ILO Working Paper 124, 27-08-2024.

Every 2 years
Hourly wages of workers with and without disabilities, international subsample
The figures
An ILO study published in 2024 found that, on average, employees with disabilities earned 12% less per hour than employees without disabilities in the international subsample analysed.
Approximately 9 percentage points could not be explained by the differences in age, education and occupation included in the model.
In that subgroup, the average pay gap reached 26%.

The ILO compares hourly wages of workers with and without disabilities in an international subsample. The analysis also estimates how much of the difference remains after considering age, education and occupation.
The 12% figure is the average for an international subsample of 30 countries. Do not attribute it to every country in the world or to all persons with disabilities.
The 12% result comes from a subsample of 30 countries, not from every country in the world.

Employment gap associated with disability
In the European Union, the employment gap between persons with and without disabilities was 24.2 percentage points in the latest update published by Eurostat in May 2026.
latest available series in the 2026 update · Eurostat, 29-05-2026.
Official European Union statistics
Eurostat, 29-05-2026
Annual
Employment rate of persons with disabilities compared with persons without disabilities
The figures
Eurostat reported in May 2026 that persons with disabilities had an employment rate 24.2 percentage points lower than that of persons without disabilities.
The data refer to the population aged 20 to 64.
The 2025 edition, with 2024 data, placed the gap at 24.0 points; the 2026 update places it at 24.2 points.

The employment gap subtracts the employment rate of persons with disabilities from the employment rate of those without disabilities. The correct unit is therefore percentage points, not a relative percentage.
Use percentage points, not ‘24.2% less’. A gap of 24.2 points compares two employment rates.
A difference expressed in percentage points should not be turned into a relative percentage without recalculating it.
